To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kinetics of directed self-assembly on chemically pattern guided substrates is significantly enhanced when compared with unguided substrates.
the kinetics of lamellar alignment in PS b PMMA block copolymer films on chemical templates is enhanced by 2-3 orders of magnitude over the kinetics of lamellae on unpatterned surfaces.

(1) the kinetics of directed self-assembly of block copolymers on chemically pattern substrates follow exponential kinetics with a barrier of 360 kJ/mol and (2) the presence of chemical guides irreversibly align lamellae.

the fundamental science behind the kinetics of directed self-assembly of block copolymers on chemical patterns, which will enable us to better understand the underlying mechanisms and optimize directed self-assembly for technological applications.
understanding how the kinetics of directed self-assembly can be controlled to produce high quality, defect-free lamellar patterns in a reasonable amount of time.

developing a fundamental understanding of how chemical guiding fields affect the kinetics of block copolymer directed self assembly and how these insights can be leveraged to improve the quality and speed of pattern formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemical guiding field provides a kinetic barrier to ordering that is significantly larger than that of a bulk film of the same composition.
chemical patterns are able to accelerate the ordering kinetics of block copolymers, but only at a cost to the equilibrium ordering morphology.

we have demonstrated that the kinetics of directed self-assembly can be directly observed in real space and real time, which provides the first step toward a fundamental understanding of the kinetics of self-assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the ability to measure the kinetics of directed selfassembly of block copolymers with unprecedented resolution in both time and space.
we have shown that chemical templates can be used to direct self assembly of block copolymers, but that there are still significant challenges in controlling the kinetics of the self assembly.

we have developed a new imaging method for real time imaging of self assembled block copolymer thin films and we have used this method to observe a new metastable morphology that is responsible for lamellar alignment in chemically patterned block copolymer films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use real space, in situ imaging of the self assembly process to understand the mechanism and kinetics of directed self-assembly.
the chemical guiding field is not only a tool to create a well ordered pattern, but it also changes the kinetics of self-assembly and the morphology of the final state.
the kinetics of directed self-assembly on chemical templates are significantly faster than on unpatterned surfaces.
